title: Evaluation of Transauricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Children and Adolescents with Hyperarousal
summary:
This study investigates whether a gentle stimulation of the auricular branch of the vagus nerve (transauricular vagus nerve stimulation, tVNS) can improve emotional and physiological regulation in children and adolescents with increased inner tension (“hyperarousal”).

Hyperarousal may present as pronounced inner restlessness, tension, irritability, or sleep difficulties. The aim of the study is to examine whether repeated tVNS in addition to a relaxation exercise (guided imagery) enhances self-regulation.

Participants receive either a combination of tVNS and guided imagery or guided imagery alone over ten consecutive days. At the beginning and end of the study, measurements of heart activity, skin conductance, and brain activity are performed. In addition, participants complete questionnaires assessing their level of tension.

The results are intended to improve the understanding of non-pharmacological treatment approaches for children and adolescents with increased inner tension.
conditions: Emotional disorders with onset specific to childhood

interventions.name:
Intervention Arm (tVNS + guided imagery)
Participants receive 10 sessions of transauricular vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) combined with standardized guided imagery over 10 consecutive days. Physiological measurements (EEG, ECG for HRV, electrodermal activity) are obtained before, during, and after

Active Control Arm (guided imagery only)
Participants receive 10 sessions of standardized guided imagery without tVNS over 10 consecutive days. Identical physiological measurements are performed on Day 1 and Day 10.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient treatment in a child and adolescent psychiatric setting.
Clinically relevant hyperarousal, defined as increased psychophysiological activation (e.g., pronounced inner tension, autonomic hyperreactivity, emotional dysregulation), based on clinical assessment during treatment.
Sufficient language and cognitive abilities to participate in questionnaires and the intervention.
Written informed consent from legal guardians and assent from the child/adolescent.
Exclusion criteria:
Neurological disorders associated with increased seizure risk or untreated epilepsy.
Implanted electronic medical devices (e.g., pacemaker).
Acute psychotic symptoms.
Severe cognitive impairment preventing participation in the intervention or assessments.
Dermatological conditions at the electrode placement site.
Concurrent participation in another interventional study.
